<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead">
You are **engine-dev-3**, the skills/agenda/producer/decider engineer on the FelsenBerry Minecraft bot-engine team. Your team-lead is the session named `felsenberry-9c` (send progress/questions with SendMessage to "felsenberry-9c"). You were respawned after a HOST REBOOT at 2026-09-03 08:46Z killed the whole team; your earlier context is gone — the repo is the ground truth.

Repo: /home/felix/ghq/github.com/felsenuboot/FelsenBerry (~/minecraft/bots is a symlink to it). READ FIRST, in this order: TODO.md (queue; items 4, 4b, 5c are yours), the "SOAK #4" section at the END of SCOREBOARD.md, the last FEEDBACK.md entry (08:55Z), GOAL.md (the human bar), then decider.js and agenda.js. Local test server is UP at 127.0.0.1:25599 (RCON 25598, password in localserver/setup.sh — RCON fixtures are sanctioned on this local server only). Ollama is up (Andy-4 model, see decider.js). An inspector bot Trail4Insp2 (port 3171, owned by team-lead) is parked on 25599 — do not use or stop it. The decider daemon is NOT running right now; start it only if you need it for a live test (`[SOAK_BOT=<name>] setsid nohup node decider.js > logs/decider.log 2>&1 &`) and tell the lead.

## Your tasks, in order

### Task 1 — TODO 4b: decider latency fix (GATES soak #5). 
Soak #4 failed the human bar on ONE criterion: direction-gate latency p50 76s (≤60 required) / p90 215s (<120 required). Attribution (verify it yourself from logs/decisions.jsonl + the `direction` records in logs/metrics-MampfManfred.jsonl, window 07:49:42Z–08:49:42Z):
- Andy's own per-call latency was 1–6.3s. But EVERY episode close sits on a 68–85s floor, including the 0ms rule decision (eid dmtl87qib1, 77s). decider.js line ~371: `if (b.owner && (dir.forMs || 0) < DRIVER_GRACE_MS) return;` with DRIVER_GRACE_MS=60000. `b.owner` comes from pids/*.meta OWNER — and since the OWNER/PURPOSE fleet-awareness law EVERY bot has an owner, so the driverless soak bot waited a driver grace no driver would ever use, then up to POLL_MS=20s.
- p90: the two `unmapped_or_unparsed` episodes (dmtl8vqp06, dmtl9yfoo10) waited PER_BOT_MIN_GAP_MS=120s before the second attempt → 215–221s.
Fix: (a) driver grace must key on an ACTUAL driver, not the OWNER label — introduce an explicit semantic (e.g. a `DRIVEN=1` spawn env recorded in the meta file / a driver-registered signal on the bot), driverless bots answer on the next poll; (b) an unparsed-reply retry rides the next POLL_MS, not the 120s per-bot gap (keep the per-bot gap for genuinely separate episodes); (c) argue briefly in FEEDBACK whether POLL_MS 20→10s for SOAK_BOT is worth it. Update spawn.sh/list.sh meta handling if you add a field (the 4-field meta format is documented in list.sh — extend, don't break older meta files). Fixture: a replay/synthetic-episode test in bench/ asserting rule-path close latency < 30s. Then `./bench/preflight.sh <port>` must stay green (216/216 expected) — spawn your own test bot for that (`OWNER=engine-dev-3 PURPOSE="4b preflight" DECIDER_EXCLUDE=1 MC_HOST=127.0.0.1 MC_PORT=25599 ./spawn.sh <FreshStupidName> 31xx --agenda`; ./list.sh first; stop it after). Bot names: always stupid/funny, ≤16 chars, never "Felsen".
Record the law-shaped lesson in FEEDBACK.md (append-only): a label added for one purpose (fleet awareness) silently changed a control-plane decision that keyed on its mere presence; presence-of-metadata gates must name the semantic they check.

### Task 2 — TODO 5c: same-remedy-repeats-across-positions escalation.
Soak #4's bot never held a tool all hour: every wood-gather attempt FROZE (ledger `frozen` wedge events); episodes opened/closed fine but the decider kept reassigning chopTrees from each new position and the bot re-froze. The frozen-repeat dedup keys on position so it can't catch it. Design + build: N same-remedy failures across positions → escalate (bigger relocate / a different remedy class); fixture cases in bench/fixtures/agenda-ladder.js; preflight green. Also diagnose the freeze itself: MampfManfred is dead but the WORLD persists on 25599 — its freeze sites were around (-20.5,108,z≈3) and (-45.4,114,z≈3); spawn a test bot there (DECIDER_EXCLUDE=1) and try chopTrees at those spots to see what wedges (R2 tooling). Report the finding to the lead before building the fix if it changes the design.

## Laws (from the team's TODO §3 — enforce them on yourself)
- Commit ONLY with explicit pathspecs (`git add <files>`; never `git add -A`/`-u`). Every commit auto-pushes via the post-commit hook; check .git/push.log if GitHub looks stale. Commit messages end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- OWNER/PURPOSE env on every spawn; DECIDER_EXCLUDE=1 on test bots; ./list.sh first, always; stop your bots when done (./stop.sh <name>).
- Ack-before-edit on any file outside your lane (decider.js, agenda.js, skills.js, producer.js, rules.json, spawn.sh meta format are yours; survival.js/metrics.mjs/bench graders are engine-dev's; SCOREBOARD.md race sections are test-driver's) — message the lead first, even for break-glass.
- Wall-clock timers/soak windows are the LEAD's job only. Never op a bot. Never touch the cavecrew server (100.101.197.44).
- FEEDBACK.md is append-only; log findings instantly, with `fix:` and `github:` lines like the existing entries.
- Report to the lead (SendMessage to felsenberry-9c) at every task boundary: what landed (commit hash), what's verified how, what you argued against and why. Your final message is your handoff report.
Start now with Task 1.
</teammate-message>

#!/bin/zsh
# bench/preflight.sh <port> — the agenda pre-flight, meant to be run on the SOAK BOT itself
# right after it comes up on a new stack and BEFORE committing to a multi-hour run.
#
# It executes nothing in the world: every case goes through __agenda.step()'s dry-run hook or
# stubs __skills.start, and each fixture restores the fields it touches. Safe on a live bot.
#
# What it is actually for: catching payload drift and stale injection in about a second. A bot
# can report the right versions in /state and still be running a half-injected stack; these
# cases exercise the real predicates, so they fail loudly when the ladder is not what you think.
# stack-check runs FIRST and checks PRESENCE, because the behavioural fixtures stub
# __skills.start and would otherwise pass green on a bot where `produce` was never installed.
set -e
PORT="${1:-3110}"
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
python3 - "$PORT" <<'PY'
import json, sys, urllib.request
port = sys.argv[1]
total = passed = 0
for f in ['stack-check', 'tier-choice', 'move-detect', 'agenda-ladder', 'agenda-deepkit', 'agenda-resume', 'agenda-idlework', 'assert-produce', 'gotoR-recovery', 'agenda-idlekit', 'agenda-hunter-route', 'agenda-escape', 'agenda-direction', 'survival-cannotheal']:
    code = open('bench/fixtures/%s.js' % f).read()
    req = urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:%s/eval' % port,
                                 data=json.dumps({'code': code}).encode(),
                                 headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
    try:
        r = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180))
    except Exception as e:
        print('%-18s UNREACHABLE %s' % (f, e)); sys.exit(1)
    if not r.get('ok'):
        print('%-18s EVAL ERROR %s' % (f, r.get('error'))); sys.exit(1)
    d = r['result']
    if d.get('skipped'):
        print('%-18s SKIPPED (%s)' % (f, d['skipped'])); continue
    if 'firePassed' in d:
        p, n, bad = d['firePassed'] + d['actPassed'], len(d['fire']) + len(d['acts']), d['failures']
    else:
        p, n, bad = d['passed'], len(d['cases']), d.get('failed') or []
    total += n; passed += p
    print('%-18s %2d/%2d %s' % (f, p, n, bad if bad else ''))
print('PRE-FLIGHT: %d/%d' % (passed, total))
sys.exit(0 if passed == total else 1)
PY

which actually mis-split as soon as a 5th field existed — fixed as part of this, see its own
comment). decider.js's driver-grace check now reads `b.driven` (from that field), not
`b.owner`; a bot with no 5th field (an older meta file, or DRIVEN simply not passed) defaults
to `driven:false` — same "assumed-false, not assumed-true" doctrine #95's frozen-repeat fix
already documents in this file for missing/ambiguous data. OWNER keeps doing exactly its
original job (fleet attribution); DRIVEN is now the ONLY thing the grace gate reads. (b) the
per-bot rate gate (`PER_BOT_MIN_GAP_MS`) is bypassed only when the CURRENT episode (same eid)
already has a recorded-but-not-yet-exhausted LLM miss (`state.llmMisses[dedupKey]`) — a
same-eid retry rides the very next poll; a genuinely new episode (different eid, no prior miss
recorded) still pays the full gap exactly as before. (c) POLL_MS 20->10s for SOAK_BOT:
NOT changed — argued below.

**Argued against, not silently skipped: (c) POLL_MS 20->10s.** With (a)+(b) landed, the
structural bound on rule-path latency is just POLL_MS itself (20s), comfortably under both the
60s p50 and 120s p90 human-bar limits with no further change — the replay fixture asserts this
directly (`POLL_MS < 30000`). Halving it buys a thinner safety margin at the cost of doubling
this decider process's own polling overhead (an httpGetJson /state round-trip per bot per
cycle) across the WHOLE fleet, not just the one soak bot under measurement, for a margin that
soak #4's own numbers don't show any need for — the floor was 68-85s BECAUSE of the two bugs

universal. The gate never asked "what do I actually need to know here?" — it asked "is this
field truthy?", and the field's truthiness stopped correlating with the question the day the
OWNER law made it always-true. Presence-of-metadata gates must name the exact semantic they
check (`driven`, a fact about the current moment) and never borrow a field whose presence
answers a different, unrelated question (`owner`, a fact about attribution) just because it is
convenient and, for now, happens to always be there. Same rot class as this file's own
"assumed-false ≠ verified-false" — an absence of information about ONE question quietly stood

input.message:
R2 diagnosis done (spawned KnautschKuno DECIDER_EXCLUDE=1 on 25599, RCON-teleported to the ledger's exact wedge coords, stopped after). Doesn't change the design you already specified — reporting per instructions, then building.

What actually happened at (-21,108,-3)/(-18,109,3), from decisions/metrics: 3 separate `restock` task_end events with outcome='wedge' (2+2+1 wedges, 4+4+2 unsticks) — genuine physics stalls (skills.js's frozenMs>6000/noProgressMs>20000 watchdog), not the leaf-litter/no-collision-block class _unstick already handles (I scanned the AABB-adjacent blocks at that spot: nothing but short_grass, which _unstick digs fine). Root condition: that whole area is heavily deforested (a whole hour of a chopping bot will do that) — only reachable trees are 15-40+ blocks away across steep terrain (bot's own y 107-109, nearest real tree canopy at y~116-119, ~9-12 block climb). chopTrees/restock's gather-search, finding nothing local, wanders wide over that terrain hunting for wood. I ran chopTrees(force:true) 3x from those exact coords: 2/3 wandered 25-40 blocks and failed CLEAN (`tool_missing`, 0 logs reached) — same shape as the (-45,114,*) site's repeated ensureTool failures (that one's the busy-rung finding, 0 wedges there, separate from this). I didn't personally reproduce a literal wedge in 3 tries — consistent with the real data too (most restock attempts at that spot didn't wedge either; 3 did out of many). Read: this is a probabilistic pathfinder stall during a long blind search over sparse/uneven terrain, not a deterministic one-block bug — there's no single terrain fix to make. That's exactly why position-based dedup can't catch it AND why a targeted terrain fix wouldn't either: the real invariant is "this neighborhood is picked clean, going back (or three blocks over) won't help." Confirms the escalation design as the right lever, doesn't change it. Building now: N same-remedy failures across positions (regardless of wedge vs clean tool_missing/acquisition_failed — same failure signature) → escalate to relocateToWork's bigger hop or a different remedy class. Fixture cases in bench/fixtures/agenda-ladder.js, preflight green after. Will report again before commit.

input.message:
Team lead asked me to hand you the exact record shape for the `remedy_escalate` ledger event I added in TODO 5c (agenda.js's new REMEDY rung), so you can grade it for soak #5. Landed in commit 16604e7 (agenda.js, swept into team-lead's commit by a shared-index race — content is mine, see TODO 5c entry / my FEEDBACK.md entry for the design writeup).

Emitted via the same two-surface discipline `dirEmit` already uses in agenda.js (`m.emit(ev, fields)` — telemetry.js's own emit, so it lands in metrics-<bot>.jsonl with the standard envelope: `{v, t, bot, run, seq, ev, ...fields}`). `ev` is literally the string `"remedy_escalate"` (NOT `"direction"` — deliberately a separate event type so it doesn't get swept into your direction-gate grader's `r.op==='open'/'close'/'promote'` filters in metrics.mjs, which only recognize those three).

Two `op` values you'll see under `ev:"remedy_escalate"`:
- `op:"fail"` — logged every time a remedy-class failure is recorded ONCE it's at or past the escalation threshold (i.e. you won't see single/below-threshold failures in the ledger, only the ones that actually mattered). Fields: `cls` (string: `"wood_gather"` or `"depot_reach"` today — chopTrees/harvestGrass/repeat-chopTrees-class PROJECT failures, ensureTool's own wood-search-came-up-empty failures, and RESTOCK's `reached:0` depot-unreachable failures all funnel into these two), `n` (the running same-class failure count), `pos` ([x,y,z] rounded ints, or null).
- `op:"escalate"` — logged once per actual escalation move dispatched (the REMEDY rung's own act()). Fields: `cls`, `n` (failure count at the moment of escalation), `tier` (1 = relocateToWork bigger-hop, 2 = directed findBlock+come to a real target), `pos`.

Both records also get a plain stdout line (`AGENDA_EVENT {"ev":"remedy",...}` — note: the STDOUT mirror uses `ev:"remedy"` not `"remedy_escalate"`, only the ledger/metrics file uses the full `"remedy_escalate"` name — grep the .jsonl file, not the console log, if you're scripting against it).

Happy to answer questions on the shape or help wire the grader if useful — just say so.

<teammate-message teammate_id="engine-dev" color="yellow" summary="Proposing 2 new fields for the direction-gate latency breakdown (task 2)">
engine-dev here, task 2: metrics.mjs's --direction-gate latency is currently a single open→close number, which is exactly why soak #4's attribution (driver-grace bug vs LLM slowness) had to be done by hand. Building a breakdown so future soaks don't need that. I'm implementing it now in metrics.mjs (my lane) using only fields that already exist — no blocking on you — but the breakdown would be more complete with two small additions to files you own. Proposing, not assuming; tell me if either is wrong-shaped or you'd rather not.

**1. decider.js — `dispatch_ms` on the decisions.jsonl record (appendDecision, ~line 536).**
Right now `latency_ms` on a rule/llm decision measures decision-COMPUTE time only (0 for rule, the Ollama call for llm) — the dirDispatch evalOn call that follows it (line ~527) isn't timed separately, so its duration is invisible, folded into the gap between one record's `t` and the next. Proposing: wrap that evalOn call with its own `const dt0 = Date.now(); ...; const dispatchMs = Date.now() - dt0;` and add `dispatch_ms: dispatchMs` to the appendDecision call at line 536 (only meaningful on src:'rule'/'llm' records that actually attempt a dispatch — skip records stay as-is). Gives me a clean "dispatch mechanics" bucket instead of inferring it.

**2. agenda.js — `standDown` on the direction 'open' event (dirEmit, openEpisode ~line 694).**
This is the more important one — ties directly to TODO 5d / test-driver's run-#6 finding (dmtlb2m212, 128665ms "latency" that was standdown carryover, not decider slowness — 5d already names this as my grader-side job: "the latency breakdown must attribute standdown carryover so it can't read as decider latency"). Today `openEpisode`'s dirEmit call has no visibility into whether the episode's own rung (`A.owner ? A.owner.id : null`, already captured as `rung`) is still cooling down from a PREVIOUS project's standDown. Proposing: at the same point, read `A.standDown[A.owner ? A.owner.id : null]` and add it as `standDown: A.owner && A.standDown[A.owner.id] > s.now ? { rung: A.owner.id, until: A.standDown[A.owner.id] } : null` to the open event's fields. That gives me `open.standDown.until` (epoch ms, same as `A.standDown[id]`'s own units) so the grader can compute `carryoverMs = max(0, min(until, close.t) - open.t)` — the exact number 5d is asking for, without hand-reading AGENDA_EVENT log lines.

Neither blocks me — my metrics.mjs code checks for both fields defensively and reports `null` with an explicit "pending" note when absent, same pattern as everything else instrumented-but-not-yet-wired in this codebase. If you land them, the breakdown upgrades automatically next run, no metrics.mjs change needed. If you'd rather do the standDown one differently (e.g. as part of your 5d fix itself, since you're touching the same code for the backoff-keying change), that's fine too — just let me know the field name/shape you land on so I read the right one.

Not touching decider.js or agenda.js myself. Full breakdown design + fixture going into FEEDBACK.md shortly.
</teammate-message>

Both of your two requested fields are landed and pushed (commit 872aa07, on top of the remedy_escalate shape I sent you earlier):

1. `decider.js`: `dispatch_ms` added to `appendDecision`'s call (same spot, ~line 536/544 now) — wrapped the `evalOn(...dirDispatch...)` call with its own timer exactly as you proposed. Present on any `src:'rule'`/`'llm'` record that reaches the dispatch step; records that returned earlier (dedup/rate-gate/frozen_repeat/driver-grace skips) never reach that code so they simply don't have the field — same "absent = not applicable" shape as everything else in that file. Verified via `bench/decider-latency-replay.js` (12/12, no behavior change) and a quick manual read of a real decisions.jsonl record.

2. `agenda.js`: `standDown` added to `openEpisode`'s `dirEmit('open', ...)` call, exactly the shape you proposed — `{rung, until}` when `A.owner`'s rung has `A.standDown[id] > s.now` at the moment the episode opens, `null` otherwise. `until` is the raw epoch-ms value from `A.standDown[id]` (same units your `carryoverMs = max(0, min(until, close.t) - open.t)` formula expects). Verified via `bench/preflight.sh`'s `agenda-direction` fixture (38/38, unaffected — additive field, nothing there asserts the open-event shape exhaustively) and a spot-check that the field actually appears/disappears correctly around a standDown window.

One thing worth knowing for your grader: this field is racy against my own 5d fix in a good way — 5d makes `A.setProject` clear the standDown the MOMENT a fresh redirect lands, so on a properly-behaving bot post-5d you should mostly see `standDown:null` on opens going forward; a non-null value now specifically flags the OLD failure mode (an episode opening before anything answered it, while a stale standdown was still blocking its own rung) rather than being a permanent feature of every open. Good for spotting a regression if 5d ever breaks, not just for backward-attributing soak #4/run #6-era data.

Let me know if either shape needs adjusting once you're actually wiring the grader against real data.

input.message:
Read the 3-death evidence closely (FEEDBACK ~09:40Z) before writing code, per your instruction, and the literal brief ("SHELTER runs before any project/kit work") doesn't actually match the failure mode — flagging why before I build something that doesn't fix the real bug.

**What actually happened, from the log timestamps:**
- Death #2: SHELTER's dig-in DID fire (09:37:38.763Z) — it just wasn't fast enough; the skeleton was already shooting from 2.5 blocks at that same moment and won the race before the dig-in finished.
- Death #3: SHELTER never fired at all, because by the time agenda.js's tick loop could evaluate anything, `dangerState` was already `'panic'` (skeleton at 1.6 blocks, ~3s after respawn). survival.js's own `shouldShelter()` (line 925) explicitly returns false on `d.state==='panic'` — "REFLEX/POSTURE already own this", by that file's own documented design. And REFLEX/POSTURE (agenda prio 0/1, both above SHELTER's 2.5) DO win arbitration whenever panic is true, full stop — no widening of SHELTER's `fire()` condition can ever preempt them, since RUNGS.find scans in prio order. So "SHELTER runs before project/kit work" is already true structurally (2.5 < 3-8.5) and isn't the actual gap.
- REFLEX's own act() just yields the body entirely to survival.js's SEPARATE internal panic-escalation ladder (BREAK_LOS/WALL_OFF/FLEE_AWAY — a mature, already-tuned system, v6 through v11 per its own header). Death #4 shows that ladder DOES work when given room (FLEE_AWAY covered real ground, HP stabilized) — the mechanism isn't broken, it just didn't win the race on #2/#3.

**So the real gap is two separate things, not one:** (1) SHELTER needs to trigger EARLIER/more aggressively in the window BEFORE panic sets in (Death #2's shape — losing a race it was already running), not "get priority over combat" (it structurally already has that, and can't/shouldn't preempt REFLEX during actual panic — I don't want to touch that ladder). (2) once genuinely spawn-camped (Death #3's shape — no proactive shelter can outrace a 3s re-engagement), the fix isn't a better shelter primitive, it's an automatic version of what you already had test-driver do BY HAND on Death #4: stop dispatching project/kit rungs entirely and let survival.js's own reactive ladder run uninterrupted until stable/dawn.

**Revised design, scoped to minimize risk to survival.js's tuned ladder:**
1. `bot._deathTimes` (bot-level, survives reinjection like `_respawnedNeedsDirection` already does) — rolling death timestamps.
2. `sense()` gains `s.recentDeaths`/`s.spawnCamped` (N=3 in M=90s, covers your exact incident with margin), `s.hostileNear` (reuses existing `s.threat.d`).
3. SHELTER's `fire()` ORs in `s.spawnCamped` and a `justRespawned && (night || hostileNear)` window — gets it starting sooner post-respawn, addressing #2's shape. Does NOT touch survival.js's panic exclusion (moot given rung ordering, and not worth the risk to a mature system).
4. `diginStandable()`'s conservative 3-deep-ground check gets a degraded fallback (dig whatever's there, 1+ deep) specifically when spawn-camped — that's your "dirt-dig fallback when no filler" ask, a narrow survival.js touch, not a ladder-logic change.
5. NEW: while `s.spawnCamped`, agenda.js suppresses PROJECT/TOOL/RESTOCK/FOOD/LIGHT/ESCAPE dispatch entirely (a guard on their `fire()`, or one gating rung above them) — automating exactly what you had the driver do manually on run #6. Clears once dawn + stable, or the death streak ages out of the window.

Item 5 is the piece I think actually matters most for a genuine spawn-camp (items 3/4 help but can't outrace a 3s re-kill) — it's also the part most likely to interact with things I don't fully see (does anything else expect PROJECT to always eventually get a turn?). Want me to build this shape, or would you rather scope it down / have engine-dev weigh in on the survival.js pieces (3/4) since it's normally their file? Not starting the build until I hear back.

Flagging a soak-hygiene miss on my end, immediately: I was live-testing TODO 5g (spawn-camp detection) on 25599 — teleported my test bot(s) to (300,90,300) via RCON, but RCON `kill` triggers a normal death/respawn, and vanilla respawn snaps back to world spawn regardless of where the bot was teleported before dying. I didn't realize that until after the fact, so my repeated kill/respawn cycles actually happened at world spawn (~(-8 to 9, 84-95, -6 to 10)) the whole time, not at the isolated coords I intended. Your ZombieFutter (TODO 5f WALL_OFF fixture) was connected at (6,95,10) during that window — ~11 blocks from where my bot kept respawning and dying, not the ≥200 the team's own soak-hygiene law asks for. I only just noticed via a `<join> ZombieFutter` log line and stopped my test bot immediately once I saw how close it was.

I don't think I directly interfered with your bot (RCON `kill` only targets the named bot, and I didn't summon anything near it), but the timing/proximity overlap is exactly the contamination shape the team already learned to watch for (soak #4's own lesson) — if your WALL_OFF/multi-threat fixture reads anything from shared world state (mob spawns, danger scoring, chat lines) during that window, or if my bot's own deaths/respawns triggered anything observable nearby, it's worth you checking whether your test data from roughly 09:57-09:59Z today is clean. Sorry for not catching this sooner — I'm done with my own live testing on 25599 now (5g's fixture cases + preflight are separately green, not affected), so no more activity from me there for now.

---
### 2026-09-03 engine-dev-3 — TODO 5g: respawn/spawn-camp handling (agenda v33)
type: fix + fixture, design revised from the original brief (reported to lead first, per their
own instruction — see the design exchange this entry summarizes)

live-verified (real tick loop, real deaths via RCON), `bench/fixtures/agenda-ladder.js` 67/67
(up from 52/52, 15 new cases), `bench/preflight.sh` 257/257 on throwaway bots (25599 only).

**Design correction, reported before building**: the literal brief ("SHELTER runs before any
project/kit work") doesn't match test-driver's own 3-death evidence (FEEDBACK ~09:40Z).
SHELTER (prio 2.5) already structurally outranks PROJECT/TOOL/RESTOCK (prio 3-8.5) — that part
was never broken. The real gaps: (a) Death #2's dig-in DID fire but lost the race to a hostile
already at 2.5 blocks; (b) Death #3's dig-in never fired because `dangerState` was ALREADY
`'panic'` by the first evaluable tick, and survival.js's own `shouldShelter()` correctly defers
to REFLEX/POSTURE (prio 0/1, which structurally outrank SHELTER too — no widening of SHELTER's
own fire() can ever preempt them) — but REFLEX just yields to survival.js's SEPARATE reactive
escalation ladder (BREAK_LOS/WALL_OFF/FLEE_AWAY, untouched here — Death #4 shows it works when
given room). Lead's ruling: build the revised shape.

**(1) `bot._deathTimes`** — a rolling death-timestamp array, bot-level not A-level (survives
re-injection, same reasoning as `#103`'s `_respawnedNeedsDirection`: a death re-injects this
whole file). **Live-caught building this**: `bot.on('death', ...)` runs at module top-level,
which means it re-registers on EVERY re-injection with nothing ever removing the old listener
— `MaxListenersExceededWarning: 11 death listeners` observed live after a handful of deaths.
The pre-existing `_respawnedNeedsDirection` handler was accidentally immune (setting the same
boolean twice is a no-op); a COUNTING handler is not — accumulated listeners meant one real
death pushed N timestamps, inflating `recentDeaths` well past reality (measured: 3 real deaths
read as 6). Fixed at the root for BOTH handlers: install exactly once per real bot object via
a `bot._deathHandlersInstalled` guard flag.

**(2) `sense()` gains `s.recentDeaths`/`s.spawnCamped`/`s.justRespawned`/`s.hostileNear`/
`s.isDay`.** The release math (raw death-count vs. the window; dawn+stable early release; the
10-minute hard cap) is factored into a PURE function, `spawnCampCheck(deathTimes, nowMs,
openedAt, isDay)`, exposed as `A._spawnCampCheck` — same discipline as `A._idleWorkOutcome`/
`A._promoteCheck` — so a fixture can drive all three release paths with SYNTHETIC timestamps,
no real wall-clock waiting for a 90s window or a 10-minute cap. `s.isDay` reuses survival.js's
own `isDaylight()` via the SAME `sv.shelter.status()` call `s.shelterActive` already made (one
call, two fields) rather than a second, independently-drifting day/night check in this file —
the exact bug class `#113`'s shared-FOODS fix just closed, avoided here from the start.

**(3) SHELTER's `fire()`** ORs in two new triggers, both explicitly NOT touching survival.js's
`d.state==='panic'` exclusion (moot given rung ordering, not worth the risk to a mature,
already-tuned system): `spawnCamped` (blanket override once genuinely camped — night/gear/
panic-state irrelevant, "something is actively killing this bot") and `justRespawned &&
surfaceExposed && (isDay===false || hostileNear)` (starts the dig-in SOONER in the pre-panic
window post-respawn, addressing Death #2's shape — losing a race it was already running).
Live-verified: RCON-killed a bot at night, isolated 300 blocks out — respawn snapped it back
to world spawn (RCON `kill` is a normal death, not a teleport-then-kill; the isolation only
held for the FIRST death of each test, a real live-test constraint worth remembering for next
time) — `rung:'SHELTER'` and `"Digging in for the night"` fired at `ticks:1`, within one 2s
tick of every single respawn.

**(5) Suppression while spawn-camped**: `SPAWN_CAMP_SUPPRESSED` (TOOL/RESTOCK/FOOD/LIGHT/
PROJECT/ESCAPE) gated in `safeFire()` — the single central point every rung's fire() already
passes through, one Set literal rather than six separate edits. Deliberately excludes REFLEX/
POSTURE/EAT_CRITICAL/SHELTER/DEPOSIT/EAT/REMEDY (combat, shelter, eating and dropping excess
inventory are not "going out to work"; REMEDY only ever fires from an ALREADY-pending failure,
and with TOOL/RESTOCK/PROJECT suppressed nothing NEW feeds it during a camp). A decider/driver
`setProject()` during suppression is NOT lost — `A.setProject` has no dependency on rung
fire(), so it still sets `A.project` and closes the direction episode exactly as always; the
project simply doesn't get its TURN to run until suppression clears, at which point its own
rung's fire() re-evaluates true against the ALREADY-set project. IDLE (the floor, never
suppressed — "zero defense must be unrepresentable") gets its own inline `spawnCamped` check in
its own `act()`: holds position instead of dispatching role-default work, since SHELTER
structurally outranks it and should own the body whenever camped, but IDLE is still reachable
if SHELTER genuinely can't act. Live-verified: 3 RCON kills in ~8s produced a single
`spawn_camp` ledger event (`op:'open', deaths:3` — confirmed the listener-leak fix, which had
initially produced two spurious `open` events for one real streak before the fix).

**Ledger**: `spawn_camp` (own event type, not folded into `direction` — a camp span isn't a
direction episode) via the same `m.emit` two-surface discipline `dirEmit` uses. `op:'open'`
(deaths, pos) / `op:'close'` (deaths, reason: `hard_cap`|`stable_dawn`|`window_aged_out`,
spanMs) — soak #5's grade can count spans and their release reason independently.

**Fixture** (`bench/fixtures/agenda-ladder.js`, 15 new cases): (A) SHELTER's widened fire() —
night-after-respawn, hostile-near-after-respawn even in daylight, and two negative cases
(safe-and-day, not-surface-exposed) proving the widening doesn't over-fire; (B) suppression —
SHELTER deliberately standing down (a real build failure) so RESTOCK/TOOL being suppressed is
actually observable rather than masked by SHELTER always outranking them anyway, plus a
sanity case proving suppression doesn't leak when not camped; (C) `A._spawnCampCheck`'s pure
release math — all three release paths (window-aged-out, dawn+stable, hard-cap) plus two
sanity baselines (below-threshold, mid-camp), all via synthetic timestamps.

**Not built**: item 4 (a degraded shallower dig-in when there's no filler AND the ground isn't
verified 3-deep — today still falls through to `no_viable_primitive` and does nothing during
a spawn camp). Sent engine-dev a concrete proposed diff for ack (cross-lane: survival.js) —
flagged a real geometric question in it myself (the cap-placement offset likely isn't correctly
parametrized for a dig shallower than 2) rather than presenting something that looks plausible
but I haven't verified against their primitive.

**Soak-hygiene note, own mistake, flagged to engine-dev directly**: RCON `kill` triggers a
normal death — respawn snaps back to world spawn regardless of where the bot was teleported
beforehand. My isolation-teleport only held for each test's FIRST death; every subsequent

engine-dev immediately. Worth remembering for future respawn-cycle live tests: isolate the
RESPAWN point (bed/anchor), not just the pre-death position.

Built exactly the revised shape from our design exchange: bot._deathTimes + bot._spawnCamp (bot-level, survives re-injection), sense() gains spawnCamped/justRespawned/hostileNear/isDay with the release math (window/dawn+stable/10-min hard cap) factored into a pure spawnCampCheck() exposed as A._spawnCampCheck for synthetic-timestamp fixture testing, SHELTER's fire() widened (spawnCamped blanket + justRespawned-and-night-or-hostile), suppression centralized in safeFire() via SPAWN_CAMP_SUPPRESSED (TOOL/RESTOCK/FOOD/LIGHT/PROJECT/ESCAPE — REFLEX/POSTURE/EAT_CRITICAL/SHELTER/DEPOSIT/EAT/REMEDY untouched), IDLE gets its own inline hold. setProject during suppression isn't lost (episode still closes, project just waits its turn). spawn_camp ledger event (open/close/reason) for soak #5.

that had just landed in the furnace's OUTPUT slot already read as "in inventory" well before
`takeOutput()` ever moved it into the player's true slots, so a before/after count taken while
the furnace window stayed open measured a zero delta on every real, successful cook (isolated

flagging so whoever eventually touches furnace auto-placement knows both callers share it.

logic exists precisely because fauna is sometimes scarce). For a bot already at/near a base
(the common case for a RESTOCK/PROJECT-anchored bot), the cooking detour costs tens of seconds;

input.message:
Cook/smelt soak-hour task done: commit `a7df20b`, 264/264 preflight, nothing near 25600 throughout (soak bot confirmed still fine, agenda:IDLE/chopTrees, right where it should be).

Built `cooked_meat` as a produce() resource — cooks whatever raw meat is already held (including chicken, since cooking is literally how a human neutralizes the raw-chicken poison risk #108 excluded from FOODS). Reused smeltCharcoal's furnace-finding shape.

**Real bug found and fixed while live-verifying** (introduced by this feature, caught before shipping): first working version reported `made:0` on every successful cook despite the raw meat genuinely being consumed and cooked items genuinely appearing. Root cause: `bot.inventory.items()` counts items sitting in an OPEN container's own slots too — a cooked item already read as "in inventory" the moment it landed in the furnace's output slot, before `takeOutput()` ever moved it to the player's true inventory, so a before/after count taken while the window stayed open always measured zero on a real success. Fixed by snapshotting before opening the furnace and reading the final count only after close(). Also found live but NOT fixed (pre-existing, inherited from smeltCharcoal, not introduced by me): furnace auto-crafting needs a table already within 4 blocks, never places one from inventory — flagged in FEEDBACK for whoever eventually touches that.

**Argument, as asked**: saturation math clearly favors cooking (roughly 2-3x hunger, 5-7x saturation over raw) when the bot can afford the stop. But I'm shipping the skill UNWIRED into FOOD's post-hunt sequence — two real architectural obstacles, not a preference call: (1) mineflayer-auto-eat's own background watcher eats raw meat on pickup independent of the agenda ladder (documented in TODO's own 5h-era law) — a hunted item can be gone before FOOD's harvest code ever sees it to hook a cook step in. (2) Even past that, EAT (prio 4) unconditionally outranks FOOD (6.5) the instant foodCount>0 — choose() hands the body to EAT the very next tick regardless of what FOOD still wants to do, a genuine priority inversion, not just a hookup detail. Proved it in a new agenda-ladder fixture case rather than just asserting it. Solving that properly needs real design work (a cooking-in-progress flag that also gates EAT, or changing what counts toward foodCount) — out of proportion to a same-session task, and exactly the class of rung-priority bug this whole session's other findings turned out to be. The skill itself is fully usable directly (`runSkill('produce',{resource:'cooked_meat',count})`) by a driver/decider/future rung right now.

bench/fixtures/producer-cook.js (new, self-calibrating like assert-produce.js, 2/2) + 1 new agenda-ladder case proving the priority-inversion. Full writeup in FEEDBACK.

Holding for the next task or the soak window closing, whichever comes first.
